To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the percentage of lymphocytes in peripheral blood is lower in MS than in controls, that lymphocyte stimulation with PHA is also lower in MS than normal, but that neither LPS stimulation or EA- and EAE-rosette formation are different from controls.
in multiple sclerosis patients with a stationary phase, the percentage of lymphocytes is significantly lower than normal.

(i) in stable patients with multiple sclerosis, the percentage of peripheral lymphocytes is lower than normal; (ii) in stable patients, lymphocyte stimulation by PHa is lower than normal, while neither LpS stimulation nor EA- or EAC-rosettes differ significantly from the normal; and (iii) during remission, the C3 serum concentration is higher than normal, but drops to normal levels during exacerbation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of immunological parameters, such as cell-mediated immunity and serum C3 concentration, in MS patients during a 1 year observation period.
the study of the immune system in multiple sclerosis (MS).
the immunological profile of MS patients in the stationary and fluctuating phases of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MS patients have an increased C3 serum concentration.

in the stable phase of MS there is no significant difference in the parameters studied from those found in normal subjects, while in the fluctuating course there is a significant increase in the concentration of the C component of complement.
the lymphocyte subpopulation and mitogen stimulation tests are not helpful for monitoring the course of MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in MS the T cell system is depressed, and the C3 component is elevated, while B cell activity is normal or slightly increased.
the immune system of patients with multiple sclerosis may be altered in a way which is not yet understood.
the immune system in multiple sclerosis is not in a hyperactive state.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in MS patients with a stable disease course, there is a significant reduction in T cell mitogen responsiveness, while the B cell mitogen responsiveness and the complement concentration in the serum is significantly elevated.
the C3 concentration in serum can be considered a useful marker for the disease activity in multiple sclerosis.
in stable multiple sclerosis patients with a lymphopenia, a defect in T cell mitogenic response to PHA can be demonstrated.
